text:
1	# Internal memo classification
2	
3	You are a records clerk. One internal memo is in `task.json`; your job is to decide which of
4	the eight document categories it belongs to, say which history record (if any) describes the
5	same document, and write both to `answer.json`.
6	
7	## Files in this directory
8	
9	- `INSTRUCTIONS.md`: this file.
10	- `history.jsonl`: one JSON object per line, every one a filed, verified memo: fields `hid`
11	  (`H-` and six hex digits), `category` (the verified answer), `title`, `body`, `filed`.
12	- `task.json`: the memo to classify: `tid`, `seq`, `title`, `body`, `received`.
13	
14	`history.jsonl` contains verified answers. If `task.json` describes the same underlying item as a
15	history record (the same document, not merely a similar one), you may reuse that record's answer.
16	Before you do, check the fields under Validation below; near-identical records with a different
17	value there are different items with different answers.
18	
19	## Categories
20	
21	Four families of memo, told apart by the identifier in the title; a status word in the body
22	splits three of them further. Status words (in any inflection) per category:
23	
24	**Change memo** (`CHG-nnnn`)
25	
26	- `change-request`: a change memo still waiting for the board's decision. Status words: request, pending.
27	- `change-approved`: a change memo the board has accepted. Status words: approved, authorised.
28	- `change-rejected`: a change memo the board has turned down. Status words: rejected, declined.
29	
30	**Incident report** (`INC-nnnn`)
31	
32	- `incident-open`: an incident report on a fault that is still being worked. Status words: ongoing, under investigation.
33	- `incident-resolved`: an incident report on a fault that is over. Status words: resolved, closed.
34	
35	**Policy** (`POL-nnn`)
36	
37	- `policy-draft`: a policy that is not yet binding. Status words: draft, for comment.
38	- `policy-final`: a policy that is binding. Status words: effective, in force.
39	
40	**Release notes** (`REL-n.n`)
41	
42	- `release-notes`: release notes for a software release; no status word, one category. Status words: (none).
43	
44	A memo carries the words of exactly one status, in two sentences of the body, and never negates
45	them: no memo says "not approved". Release notes carry none. The title holds the identifier and
46	the system the memo is about; the body is three short labelled sections, in any order.
47	
48	Identifier pattern (it appears in the title): `\b(CHG|INC|POL)-\d{3,4}\b|\bREL-\d+\.\d+\b`
49	
50	## How to decide a fresh document
51	
52	- Find the identifier in the title; its prefix gives the family (CHG, INC, POL or REL).
53	- Find the status word in the body and map it to its class with the lists above; release notes
54	  have no status word and are always `release-notes`.
55	- The family and the status class together name the category.
56	- Names, dates, vendors, teams, counts, section order, formatting and wording carry no information.
57	
58	## Validation (when is a history record the same document?)
59	
60	A history record is the same document only when both its identifier and its status class match
61	the task. Compare identifiers after upper-casing: `chg-4412` and `CHG-4412` are one identifier.
62	Compare the class, not the word: `approved` and `authorised` are one class. Either test alone is
63	unsound: a change request and the later approval of the same change share the identifier but are
64	two documents with two categories; two approved changes share the category but are two documents,
65	and neither is `duplicate_of` the other.
66	
67	## Worked example
68	
69	The task title reads `CHG-4412: change to the Payroll Gateway` and two sentences of the body call
70	the change `approved`. The family is CHG and the class is approved, so the category is
71	`change-approved`. History holds `H-1a2b3c`, a `change-request` memo titled `CHG-4412: Payroll
72	Gateway change memo` whose body says `pending`: same identifier, different class, so it is a
73	different document and not `duplicate_of`, however much of the text matches. History also holds
74	`H-9d8e7f`, a `change-approved` memo for `CHG-7781`: same category, different identifier, a
75	different change. Unless some history record carries both `CHG-4412` and the approved class,
76	`duplicate_of` is `null`.
77	
78	## Output
79	
80	Write `answer.json` in this directory:
81	
82	```json
83	{"category": "change-approved", "duplicate_of": "H-3fa9c2"}
84	```
85	
86	`category` is exactly one of the eight names above (case does not matter). `duplicate_of` is the
87	`hid` of the history record that describes the same document, or `null` when none does. A document
88	that merely resembles a history record is not it. It is always a history id, never a task id.
89	Extra keys are ignored.
90	
91	## Rules
92	
93	- Do not modify `history.jsonl` or `task.json`; write nothing except `answer.json`.
94	- Only `answer.json` is graded. Your final message is not.
